items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the education law, in relation to the salary of certain teachers providing instruction in career and technical education to school age students
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S1469

 TITLE OF BILL :  An act to amend the education law, in relation to
the salary of certain teachers providing instruction in career and
technical education to school age students

 PURPOSE :

To provide adequate funding at BOCES component school districts for
career and technical education teachers.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section 1 amends the education law relating to salaries for teachers
providing instruction in career and technical education to school age
students for the 2016-2017, 2017-2018, 2018-2019, 2019-2020, 2020-2021
school years.

Section 2 provides the effective date.

 JUSTIFICATION :

This bill improves resources and programming for career and technical
education to school age students. New York State provides aid to
school districts to help them pay for services that they purchase from
BOCES, including teachers for instruction in career and technical
education. There is, however, a cap on teacher salaries which has not
been increased since 1991. Since then, New York has highlighted career
and technical education as a priority for preparing students for work
and college in the 21st century. This bill updates aid to match the
state's educational priorities in BOCES component school districts.

The expansion of Career and Technical Education (CTE) programs is
essential. For many students, CTE offers the most promising pathway to
career success. Funding and reimbursement structures, particularly
BOCES and Special Services Aids, needs improvement and expansion so
that all students may benefit from its programs. By facilitating
broader investments and public-private partnerships in these areas, we
can present an integrated career and technical curriculum to students.

As stated, the current aid formula for BOCES CTE programs has not
changed since 1990. The state only provides aid for the first $30,000
of a BOCES instructor's salary. This has the effect of reducing state
support for CTE programs and shifting the costs to local schools.
What results is the underinvestment of high-quality programs that
provide students with the skills employers demand. According to SED,
more than 90% of CTE students graduate with a Regents diploma, some
with Advanced Designation. By increasing the aidable salary for all
CTE programs this bill will significantly improve CTE services and
programs to students.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

2015-2016: 5.7920 Passed the Senate.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

To be determined.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect immediately.
